content.rendered:
Bruce was fascinated with traditional American folk and gospel long, long before the Seeger Sessions.

Although it took until his 2006 album for us to hear Bruce’s arrangements, we’d occasionally catch a glimpse through live tracks like “This Land is Your Land,” and compilation releases like “We Shall Overcome.”

But way back in the autumn of 1981, Bruce was tinkering with the classic gospel hymn “Precious Memories,” and he happened to capture it on tape–and that tape happened to leak. Take a listen to the fascinating one-minute, double-tracked snippet below. (That’s all that we have.)

It’s difficult if not impossible to judge from the recording if there was a particular version that influenced Bruce to tackle “Precious Memories.” Dozens of artists have covered it going back to the 1920s (it was written by J.B.F. Wright in 1935) in a variety of styles. Sister Rosetta Tharpe’s version was one of the more prominent early recordings…

but given Bruce’s country-ish arrangement, it’s possible that Willie Nelson’s version (released in 1976) was at least somewhere in mind.

In any event, as far as we know, Bruce never recorded “Precious Memories” in full and has never covered it live, so we’re left to wonder what he might have done with it with a band as talented as he assembled for the Seeger Sessions.

Precious Memories
Recorded: September-December 1981 (demo only)
Never performed live

© September 5, 2018

excerpt.rendered: Sometime in late 1981, Bruce sat down with a tape recorder and attempted a cover of “Precious Memories.” Listen to that demo here.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cover Me, Precious Metal: Two Hearts
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Check out Precious Metal's hard-driving, power pop rendition of "Two Hearts," approved by The Boss himself (or so we're told).

jetpack-related-posts.title: Where the Band Was: Verona, October 5, 2006
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: My all-time favorite show--under a full moon, in an ancient arena, Bruce breathed new life into a collection of American folk songs and shared them with a raucous but respectful Italian crowd.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Heaven’s Wall
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Who the heck would ever think to combine samba rhythm, middle eastern melody, a self-guitar duel, discordant strings, cowbell, and a gospel choir? Bruce Springsteen, that's who!

jetpack-related-posts.title: Satan’s Jeweled Crown
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In the spring of 1993, Bruce leaned further into his new band's strengths with their gorgeous cover of a country-gospel classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: October 16
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Bruce debuts "Long Time Comin'" nine years before its album release, a star-studded show at the Roxy, Bruce and Billy Joel perform for Barack Obama, and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Living on the Edge of the World
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Living on the Edge" is a glorious hot mess of a song. An unreleased outtake until 1998, it nevertheless spawned no less than three officially released Springsteen originals along the way.
